articleTitle: A Second-Order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC With Passive Integrator and Active Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The paper introduces a novel second-order noise-shaping circuit structure for designing high-resolution and low-power consumption Noise-Shaping Successive Approximation Register (NS SAR) Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs). This circuit utilizes an amplifier with a gain of 5 and two passive integrators to enhance the in-band noise attenuation through second-order noise shaping. The paper also investigates the impact of gain error in the dynamic amplifier on the resolution of the ADC. By achieving a Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio (SNDR) of 92.9 dB peak across a bandwidth of 0.5 MHz, the effectiveness of the proposed circuit structure is verified. Overall, this research presents a promising approach for designing NS SAR ADCs with improved resolution and reduced power consumption, offering potential benefits in various applications that require high-performance analog-to-digital conversion.

articleTitle: Power Analysis based on Deep Learning for Multiple Implementations of Cryptographic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Power analysis is a side-channel method widely studied and proven effective in attacks. Deep learning-based power analysis can extract higher-level and more abstract features from power traces, enabling attacks on cryptographic devices with protective measures. There are many types of neural networks used in deep learning, and this paper applies various neural networks to power analysis of Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm implementations on Microcontroller Unit (MCU) and Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The results show that for implementations of cryptographic algorithms with no or weak protection, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and CNN-LSTM networks all demonstrate good attack effectiveness. When the training set is insufficient, CNN and CNN-LSTM perform better. For unsecured or first-order fixed mask-implemented cryptographic algorithms, simple network structures can also achieve good attack results.

articleTitle: PPM: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Intelligent Medical Diagnosis Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The extensive utilization of deep learning techniques has significantly boosted the efficacy of intelligent Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) using medical data from multiple modalities. Deep learning techniques generally suffer from high computational complexity and cloud computing can effectively empower deep learning techniques by optimized software (e.g. distributed training/inference) and specific hardware (e.g. GPUs, FPGAs and TPUs). However, cloud computing also increases the risk of medical data leakage, which greatly hurts patients’ privacy. There has been several techniques including homomorphic encryption approach proposed to preserve patients’ privacy. However, none of them can be directly applied to deep neural networks to improve medical CAD applications via multi-modal data fusion. In this paper, we propose PPM, a framework integrating semantic level multi-modal data fusion neural network with homomorphic encryption mechanism, in order to preserve patients’ privacy while maintaining the diagnostic performance. We conduct experiments on multi-source and multi-modal medical data for Upper Gastrointestinal (UGI) cancer screening.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Structure for Concatenated Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Erasure codes play an important role in improving network performance. Adding erasure codes to QUIC can effectively reduce data retransmission times, leading to better network performance. However, the complexity of the RS codes used in QUIC-FEC is high. Using short polar codes can reduce complexity. However, short polar codes have poor erasure correction performance. To solve this problem, we first proposed a method of combining (7, 4) Hamming codes with short polar codes in parallel. After providing protection for the incompletely polarized channels, the performance was significantly improved while maintaining low complexity and delay. Subsequently, based on Tanner diagrams of polar codes and Monte Carlo simulations, we determined the key bits that had the significant impact on the performance of the parallel concatenated codes. Therefore, we proposed a new parallel-serial hybrid structure, using (7, 4) Hamming codes to provide additional protection for these key bits. The results showed that the performance of the hybrid concatenated codes was better than that of the parallel concatenated codes, even better than the polar codes with the same bit rate and nearly twice the length of hybrid concatenated codes. The hybrid scenario also outperformed the RS codes used in QUIC protocol to restore lost packets. This new hybrid concatenated scheme can also be directly extended to a wider range of component codes.

articleTitle: Design, Implementation, and Research of Non-Linear Boolean Functions in Sequence Cryptography Based on AIC Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In cryptography, the design and implementation of sequence cryptography algorithms are challenging due to the complex structure of Non-Linear Boolean Function (NLBF) and limitations of available reconfigurable resources. This makes sequence cryptography as a top topic in cryptography. This paper systematically analyzes 49 sequence cryptography algorithms, and summarizes characteristics of the number of XOR terms, AND terms, input ports, and variables, basing on their NLBF. This paper investigates the characteristics of the And-Inverter Cones(AICs) logic units and cluster units, analyzes the AICs structure's capability in implementing nonlinear Boolean functions in stream ciphers, and proposes a high-performance, low-resource utilization design scheme for a reconfigurable non-linear Boolean function operation unit. From experimental verification, the logic synthesis tool ABC concludes that the AICs structure is more suitable for the reconfigurability of NLBF compared to the traditional Look-Up Table (LUT) structure. Comparing to the traditional LUT structure, the ABC results show there is 39.8% reduction in delay and 23.2% reduction in area.

articleTitle: A ECA Fusion Smoke Detection Algorithm and Prototype Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Currently, environmental authorities primarily regulate black smoke emissions from vehicles by sampling and testing exhaust gases using smoke meters. This regulatory method is inefficient and can pose significant health risks to testing personnel when employed for extended periods. The advancements in deep learning offer a new direction for black smoke vehicle detection; however, existing solutions have not achieved optimal results. To address issues such as excessive computational complexity and inadequate datasets, this paper employs data augmentation techniques to expand the dataset. We enhance the YOLOV8 network by incorporating depth-wise separable convolutions and attention mechanisms, presenting a lightweight object detection algorithm, YOLOV8 (ECA), deployed on edge computing devices. This algorithm achieves a detection frame rate of 20FPS on Jetson devices with a black smoke vehicle recognition rate of up to 95.57%.

articleTitle: Prefabricated Construction Supply Chain Management Based on Improved Hierarchical Finite State Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Prefabricated constructions have gained global popularity due to their inherent advantages. To enhance the efficiency and coordination of the supply chain process, this study introduces the concept of hierarchy and proposes an event-driven Hierarchical Finite State Machine (HFSM) model. By establishing a mapping relationship between material state and FSM, the model enables scientific hierarchical management of the prefabricated construction supply chain. This is achieved through the implementation of a connection function (state filter function) that links different levels of state machines. The practical application of the HFSM model is demonstrated using three sequential stages: Procurement, Delivery, and On-site Installation. Through the customization of vector T and function g, the HFSM can be flexibly expanded and modified to adapt to different project management modes. The proposed model enhances information coordination among all stakeholders in the prefabricated supply chain, enabling hierarchical management at strategic, tactical, and operational levels. Furthermore, future research can leverage large-scale labeled data and belief networks to improve the model’s performance and achieve even more promising outcomes.

articleTitle: Simulink Modeling and Performance Verification of 2.4-GHz Fractional-N Reference Oversampling PLL with 20-MHz Loop Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Simulink model for a mixed-signed 2.4 GHz fractional-N reference Oversampling Phase-Locked Loop (OSPLL) to meet the requirements of modern wireless communication equipment that require low noise specific frequency clocks. The proposed OSPLL uses Bang-Bang Phase Detectors (BBPD) with an Oversampling Rate (OSR) to improve the equivalent reference frequency, and a Digital-To-Time Converter (DTC) to reduce the impact of high-frequency shaped noise in fractional-N mode. We verify the proposed OSPLL using MATLAB Simulink, and it achieves a Root-Mean-Square (rms) jitter of 303 fs in fractional-N mode with a loop bandwidth of 20 MHz when the reference frequency is 60 MHz and OSR is 40.

articleTitle: Design of Tile-based ARGB Image Lossless Compressor and Decompressor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The utilization of lossless compression is an essential technique, and the compression and decompression of images without any loss have consistently remained a prominent subject of research. In the field of chip design, such as GPU and AI, memory access often becomes a bottleneck for system performance. The frequent read and write operations on color buffer data have a significant impact on performance. This paper aims to improve memory access efficiency by reducing the amount of data accessed in the color buffer from the perspective of data compression. However, with the development of the gaming and special effects industries, GPUs need to process images rendered with special effects. Existing algorithms are good at compressing natural images but have poor compatibility and suboptimal compression ratio for this type of image. In this paper, we first design the QOI+ algorithm based on the Quite Ok Image (QOI) algorithm, which is good at dealing with the compression of non-natural images. Then, we propose a fusion optimization algorithm called QOI++, which covers both natural images and synthetic images. We provide a dedicated accelerator for QOI++ compression and decompression, which conforms to the AXI4-Stream interface. It can be selected for compression of tile sizes of 4x4, 8x8, and 16x16. The compression ratio achieved are 48.72% for 4x4 tiles, 41.22% for 8x8 tiles, and 38.60% for 16x16 tiles, with a clock frequency of 400MHz.

articleTitle: A 12-bit 1MS/s SAR ADC with Buffers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: A 12-bit Successive Approximation Register(SAR) Analog-to-digital Converter(ADC) with 1MHz sampling rate is used in the front-end amplifier of optical receiver to monitor parameters such as DC flow, AC amplitude and temperature. The circuit integrates a 12-bit SAR ADC core circuit, input buffer and reference voltage buffer. The DAC array in this design adopts a Capacitance-Resistor(C-R) hybrid array, which adopts a capacitance structure at 8 Most Significant Bits(MSBs) and adopts a resistor structure at 4 Least Significant Bits(LSBs), and uses a Vcm-based switching strategy. The ADC is implemented using a SiGe 90nm BiCMOS process with a supply of 3.3V and a reference voltage of 2.5V. For 1 MS/s sample rate, this ADC achieves up to 11.5 Effective Number of Bits(ENOBs).

articleTitle: Conceptual Analysis of Information Graphics Design in the Context of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This article conceptually distinguishes between visually generated information by artificial intelligence and human-designed information graphics, and proposes the differentiation of information graphics concepts in the context of artificial intelligence and their distinguishing criteria from visualized information. It provides theoretical support for the continuous development of visually generated designs by artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: A SAR-Based Fast Automatic Digital Calibration Circuit of On-Chip Clock
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The clock signal is a critical factor for digital circuits. However, during the chip manufacturing process, variations in conditions such as power supply voltage, process, temperature, and more can lead to deviations in oscillators frequency compared to the design specifications, the value may even reach a variation range of ± 35%, which potentially impact the functionality and performance of the chip. In order to compensate the influence of these non-ideal factors on the oscillator frequency. An on-chip fast digital automatic calibration with Successive Approximation Register (SAR) logic is proposed, compared with the traditional logic of calibration by addition and subtraction, the proposed circuit can exhibit high calibration speed. 8-bit control word on-chip fast digital automatic calibration module of proposed is designed in TSMC 180nm process, and the proposed calibration scheme has been applied to the actual chip to verify the reliability of the designed scheme, which has an important impact on the use of the internal clock of the chip.

articleTitle: Multi-Lable Wafer Defect Pattern Classification Using ResNet-based Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Wafer testing is a pivotal stage in enhancing semiconductor manufacturing efficiency. Wafer testing is a critical step in determining the quality of chips manufactured on wafers and plays a vital role in chip yield assessment. The results of wafer needle testing are used to generate a Wafer Bin Map(WBM) by analyzing WBMs, enabling the identification of defective wafers. This paper presents an approach for the classification of WBMs. In the preprocessing stage, it employs an adaptive OPTICS-based circular graph filtering algorithm to automatically determine optimal OPTICS parameters. Afterwards, three types of ResNet-based neural network are then employed for Wafer Defect Pattern Classification, resulting in improved accuracy. For the learning rate is 0.01, the classification accuracy reaches the maximum at 97.6%.

articleTitle: Classification of Stock Information Disclosure Level Based on SVM and CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Information disclosure is an important measure of stock market supervision, but the information characteristics of each listed company are varied, so how to classify and predict the information disclosure level of the company is a challenging task. In this paper, an information disclosure evaluation method of A-share listed companies based on One-Class Support Vector Machine (One-Class SVM) and Convolution Neural Network (CNN) models are proposed. The samples of D level companies (i.e., companies with unqualified information disclosure level) are insufficient, and they are the focus of supervision, so this paper adopts One-Class SVM to identify them from the other types of companies in the first place. Further, for other levels A, B and C (i.e., companies with qualified information disclosure level), the number of samples is relatively large, so the CNN classification method is adopted. By selecting nearly 2,000 stocks in the main board of A-shares as research objects, they are divided into training sets and test sets, and the model is trained according to various indicators of listed companies. Finally, the classification accuracy of the D category is about 81%, meeting the needs of market supervision.

articleTitle: A Shadow Detection Method Based on Neural Network in PCBA Height Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In Fringe Projection Profilometry (FPP) systems, the shadow caused by the object which results in the occluded area without fringe pattern will lead to the reconstruction errors. In particular, in Printed Circuit Board Assembly(PCBA) height measurement applications, its complex surface characteristics and other phenomena such as secondary reflection of projected light increase the difficulty of shadow detection. In this paper, we propose a shadow detection method combining neural network model and image post-processing. This method obtains feature images containing shadow through a multi-directional fringe projection system. A neural network model is trained by extracting neighborhood features of shadow points, and then the output of the network is checked by a post-processing algorithms to complete shadow detection. The results of the experiments show that the Mean Intersection Over Union (MIoU) value of this method is 0.9205, and the Misclassification Error (ME) value is 0.0064, which are better than the state of art method and meets the actual inspection requirements.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Current Sensing Front-End IC Design for Wide-Range Dynamic Current Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper presents a high-precision front-end Integrated Circuit (IC) for wide-range dynamic current detection. Traditional current detection circuits usually employ the topology with linear transconductance for current detection, which is limited in its ability to accommodate large signal variations. We propose a multi-range detection method to address this issue. To amplify the input current into a voltage signal, the input current is divided into multiple ranges, and then it is amplified into a voltage signal using corresponding current-to-voltage conversion circuits. The circuit is designed in TSMC 0.18μm-CMOS process. The power supply voltage is 3.3 V. The results show that the designed circuit is capable of detecting current in a dynamic range from 1nA to 100μA, with a maximum detection error of 0.848%.

articleTitle: OWI Controller with FIFO Buffer Function Based on AHB-Lite Bus
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper proposes a One-Wire (OWI) digital communication interface with asynchronous First in First out (FIFO) buffering function based on Advanced High-performance Bus (AHB-Lite), which adopts half-duplex mode to realize networking communication between host and multiple slaves. Based on this design, the interface can be specifically configured by the AHB-Lite bus for data, with reading interface status information, and supports parity and glitch filtering filter functions. In order to realize the stability of single-wire communication with external OWI devices in the data transceiver module, the asynchronous FIFO buffer function is added. During the data transmission process, FIFO can buffer single-threaded data. The finite state machine method is used to control the transmission timing of the OWI interface, and Register Transfer Level (RTL) simulation is carried out, which shows that the design can reduce the use of hardware resources and has good practicability.

articleTitle: Technology Generic Delta-Sigma ADC Design with gm/ID Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In contrast to traditional Operational Transconductance Amplifiers (OTAs), ring amplifiers present notable advantages in terms of superior performance and ease of scaling, rendering it a favored choice in analog circuit design. However, it is hard to use traditional hand-calculation in determining its optimal sizing, posing a substantial challenge for designers in sizing the ring amplifier. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a systematic gm/ID-based design method for the self-biased ring amplifier, which is automated within the analog design tool TED. The feasibility of the design procedure is verified through simulations using 65nm and 180nm technologies. Furthermore, the proposed design methodology is applied to a practical Delta-Sigma Modulator (DSM) design, resulting in over 100dB SNDR and 100kHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 10GS/s 7b Time-Interleaved Time-Domain ADC with Speed-Enhanced Bootstrapped Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel 10-GS/s 7-bit time-interleaved time-domain Successive Approximation Register (SAR) Analog-To-Digital Converter (ADC) that utilizes a speed-enhanced bootstrapped switch and a triple-latch comparator. The proposed ADC comprises a 4-way time-domain ADC that employs the constant current source charge Voltage-To-Time Converter (VTC) and the 7-bit SAR Time-To-Digital Converter (TDC) for medium resolution and high conversion speed. Unlike conventional approaches, an additional passive discharge path is utilized to improve the settling time of the switch while reducing the parasitism of the critical path. To further enhance the ADC conversion speed, the triple-latch feed-forward comparator operates in parallel to the TDC delay cell, eliminating its timing from the critical loop. The prototype was fabricated using a 65nm CMOS process, and simulation results demonstrate an SNR of 40.12 dB and an SFDR of 50.08 dB at a conversion rate of up to 10-GS/s and input frequency up to 4.41-GS/s.

articleTitle: A DCA Attack Scheme and a Genetic Algorithm-based Intelligent Fault Injection Algorithm For White-Box AES Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In this paper we attack the white-box AES implementation with Differential Correlation Analysis (DCA) and fault injection, which are major risks the white-box AES implementation is facing now. A differential computation analysis (DCA) attack strategy is presented targeted at the implementation of the white-box AES algorithm based on a combination T-box. Using the DCA attack method, 16 subkeys are extracted successfully, which underscores the presence of a notable side-channel security vulnerability within the white-box AES encryption scheme. In order to improve the protection ability of the scheme against side-channel attacks, the enhanced rotating S-box masking scheme is adopted. No security risk has been detected which proves the validity of the mask scheme. Moreover, this research performs the fault injection attack on white-box implementation. However, the process typically demands substantial time and resources due to its manual testing nature. To optimize the method, we introduce an intelligent fault injection algorithm utilizing a genetic algorithm, which automates the fault injection attack to white-box implementation. This proposed scheme exemplifies intelligence and automation in the testing process. The empirical comparison highlights that the automated fault injection algorithm significantly enhances attack efficiency by 980% when compared to the random parameter search method.

articleTitle: Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm on Dynamic Segment of FlexRay Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: FlexRay is a critical communication protocol in automotive electronic systems to achieve high reliability and realtime data transmission. This paper introduces an improved particle swarm algorithm for the FlexRay dynamic segment, which can provide a suitable message scheduling table for given FlexRay networks to meet the increasingly complex scenarios of practical applications and improve network performance overall. Bus utilization and worst-case response time are the key roles in the dynamic segment scheduling of FlexRay. By conducting experiments based on MATLAB, the network performance, which includes the bus utilization and the worst-case response time, has effectively improved according to experimental results.

articleTitle: An UVM-Based Verification Platform for Hardware and Software Co-Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: As chips grow in size and complexity, functional verification in a software environment is increasingly unable to meet the needs of efficient chip production processes. Therefore, the improvement of verification efficiency becomes critical. For the bus subsystem including AXI, AHB, AXI2AHB-bridge and AHB2APB-bridge, a coverage-driven Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) hardware and software co-simulation verification platform is built by taking advantage of the high-speed performance and object oriented programming of the Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) hardware platform, which effectively improves the verification efficiency of Intellectual Property (IP) cores based on AXI, AHB and APB protocols and reduces the development cycle.

articleTitle: Hardware Design of PQC Classic McEliece Finite Field Operations and Encryption Module
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: The security of existing cryptosystems mostly relies on the difficulty of solving integer factorization problems and discrete logarithm problems. However, in recent years, with the rapid development of quantum computers, the time required to solve these difficult problems has been significantly reduced, which will pose significant risks to the transmission of information. Post-quantum algorithms are a type of cryptographic algorithm specifically designed to resist quantum computer attacks. The National Institute of Standards and Technology of the United States(NIST) has completed four rounds of selection work from 2016 to 2022. The Classic McEliece algorithm is the only Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithm that has been selected for the fourth round of selection after more than 50 years. However, currently, the research and implementation of this algorithm are mostly focused on the software algorithm level, while the hardware implementation can be said to be very few. At the same time, hardware-implemented cryptographic algorithms have certain advantages in terms of security, algorithm execution speed, and other aspects compared to software. In this paper, the arithmetic part and the encryption part of the Classic McEliece algorithm are designed, and a UVM verification platform is built to verify its functionality. Finally, the hardware circuit is verified on the SAKURA-G FPGA development board, relevant resource consumption was collected and compared with the work of the predecessors.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Level Shifter with Wide Voltage Range and Low Delay
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: Level shifters are the most important interface circuits in multi-source systems. In this paper, a two-supply bidirectional level shifter with a wide voltage range and low delay is designed using 95nm BCD process. The proposed level shifter can operate within the voltage shifting range of any combination of supply voltages. The proposed level shifter uses latches and a cascaded cross-coupled pair for pull-up network, which significantly enhances the speed and dynamic power consumption performance. Simulation comparison results show that the proposed circuit is functional for the full supply voltage range(1–6V). The rise delay and dynamic current is reduced to less than 2.06ns and 0.36μA for voltage up-conversion from 1V to 6V, and less than 0.2ns and 0.33μA for voltage down-conversion from 6V to 1V.

articleTitle: Residual Dense Network with an Attention Mechanism for Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In response to the common problems of incomplete dehazing and color distortion in existing image dehazing algorithms, this paper proposes an image dehazing algorithm based on attention mechanism and residual dense network. Firstly, design a shallow feature extraction module that uses multi-scale convolutional kernels to extract texture information of different scenes. Secondly, based on the encoding decoding model, a network structure is constructed using residual dense blocks and global residual connections, and combined with a dual channel attention mechanism module for feature fusion and extraction. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity compared to mainstream dehazing algorithms, and has good dehazing performance.

articleTitle: A 85/215/430 KHz 3rd-Order Active-RC Low-Pass Filter with a Fast Automatic Frequency Tuning for a Zero-IF Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In this paper, a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order active-RC Low-Pass Filter (LPF) is proposed for a zero-IF receiver. The LPF enables 85/215/430 KHz passband selection and 3 dB per step gain adjustment from 0 to 45 dB. In order to deal with the deviation of the filter cut-off frequency caused by process variation, an automatic frequency tuning circuit is applied to the filter, which can cover the RC value variation of ±40%. The low-pass filter circuit is implemented in 55 nm CMOS process. The measurement results show that when the cut-off frequency is 85/215/430 KHz, the rejection at 485/615/830 KHz is 48/32/24 dB respectively. The passband ripple is 1.2/0.3/2.5 dB respectively. The filter consumes 2.5 mA from 2 V supply. The area of the filter circuit is 350 um × 750 um.

articleTitle: A Multi-Channel Low-Power LED Driver Circuit for PPG
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper introduces a precision current rudder type LED constant current driver with a 8-Bit dynamic range adjustable DAC, and a 2-bit programmable full scale option. It can be flexibly configured to meet the requirements of LED brightness for photoelectric volume pulse acquisition in different cases. The 180nm CMOS process realizes current configuration in the 0–128mA range, with a single 1 LSB input resulting in a 125–500μA current change. The LED drive current amplitude is controlled by the combination of binary and thermometer code. This work achieves a system power consumption of 0.386 mW through low-voltage logic circuits and low-power operational amplifiers. It adopts Chopper Offset-Stabilized Opamp to solve the problem of offset and noise.

articleTitle: Evaluating Side-Channel Attack Vulnerabilities in Post-Quantum CRYSTALS-Kyber Hardware Based on Simple Power Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: CRYSTALS-Kyber is a new algorithm that the NIST recently selected to standardize public-key encryption and key establishment. Therefore, studies are needed to evaluate the side-channel attack resistance of CRYSTALS-Kyber implementations. This paper presents a simple power analysis of a CRYSTALS-Kyber hardware implementation with the security parameter k=3. Since hardware implementations perform computations in parallel, the power consumption of each operation is difficult to quantify. The entire power consumption trace was identified using 6,072,500 samples during the CCAKEM implementation of Kyber. A significant part of the message encoding power consumption occurred during decapsulation. These findings show that existing hardware implementations of CRYSTALS-Kyber require effective countermeasures to efficiently resist side-channel attacks.

articleTitle: A 2nd-Order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC with Reused Dynamic Amplifier Assisted Integrator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In this paper, a Successive Approximation Register (SAR) Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) with standard 2nd-order Noise-Shaping (NS) function is proposed. The design employs a ping-pong structure and a reused closed-loop dynamic amplifier to realize the 2nd-order noise shaping, which effectively reduces the non-ideal factors such as in-band quantization noise, comparator noise and others. This can significantly improve ADC accuracy and improve power efficiency. The SAR ADC proposed in this paper utilizes V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CM</inf>-based switching scheme and bottom sampling to reduce the impact of charge injection while reducing dynamic power consumption. The proposed architecture is designed in 180 nm CMOS technology, which realizes a peak Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio (SNDR) of 69.3 dB at sampling frequency of 32 MS/s, and Schreier Figure of Merit (FoM) reaching 159.8 dB.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient and Area-Saving Capacitor Switching Scheme for SAR ADCs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper presents a switching strategy to diminish energy consumption and minimize the capacitance area overhead in Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-Digital Converter (SAR ADC). The Power Area Dual Saving (PADS) switching scheme combines bottom plate sampling technology and a novel switching method, saving the highest and second highest capacitors in CDAC and eliminating the power consumption of the first two conversion cycles. At the same time, this switch scheme only switches for a single capacitor each time (except for the first conversion), greatly reducing the complexity of the switch-switching logic. Compared with traditional switching schemes, this scheme reduces the area of capacitor by 75% and the switching power consumption by 97.7%. To verify the feasibility of this switching strategy, a high-precision 14-bit SAR ADC was used for validation in this paper. The results indicate that this strategy can effectively demonstrate its advantages in energy efficiency and chip area overhead.

articleTitle: Unequal Error Protection Coding Scheme in Semantic Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper presents a text semantic communication system that learns the semantic importance of data through a pre-trained neural network and divides semantic information into three layers based on semantic importance. Then unequal error protection (UEP) schemes are constructed using Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes of length-31 and length-63. Finally, UEP schemes are applied to the text semantic communication system, and the simulation results indicate that the text average similarity can reach above 92%. Simulation shows that it can improve the transmission reliability of important data, that is, reduce the bit error rate of important data transmission, and further improve the reliability and effectiveness of wireless communication while maintaining complexity.

articleTitle: A Design of Homogeneous Multi-Core SoC with General-Purpose Floating-Point Processors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In the era of big data and artificial intelligence, SoC design for computationally intensive applications are a huge challenge, especially for general-purpose processors where the underlying architecture is single-core in nature. This paper exploits customized general-purpose floating-point processors to build a homogeneous multi-core SoC. The general-purpose floating-point processor supports the IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point standard and has effective circuit implementation of matrix operations. The SoC integrates a micro-controller compatible with Microblaze instruction set and a floating-point arithmetic module composed of various functional IPs, which makes the presented homogeneous multi-core SoC programmable and flexible. The homogeneous multi-core SoC is built using a three-layer network-on-chip, and the general-purpose floating-point processor is mounted on the network-on-chip node. Finally, matrix multiplication mapping is implemented on this homogeneous multi-core SoC for performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Design of Octal Half-Bridge Motor Driver with Serial Input Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: This paper presents an 8-channel, half-bridge DMOS output driver controlled by Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI). The driver has 8-channel outputs, with up to six simultaneous outputs. By changing the output load and adjusting the SPI setting, full-bridge output or half-bridge output can be selected. And the serial interface clock frequency is up to 5MHz. Moreover, the driver equips with Short Circuit Protection (SCP), Under Voltage Protection (UVP), and thermal shutdown, which can timely alarm and protect the circuit in case of abnormal working conditions. The Driver is designed in DongBu HiTek (DBH) 0.18 um BCD process with the 5V and 55V Dual power supply voltage. The operating input range of the driver is between 9 to 55V, and the gate voltage of output MOSFET pair is increased through high-voltage charge pump technology, resulting in an output voltage of up to 55V. At a working voltage of 55V, the simulation results show that the on-state resistance of the bridge arm is less than 2 ohms, the start-up time is 173.8us, the working current is 0.8A, and the peak current can reach 1.3A. It can be applied to automotive and industrial loads as well as DC motors.

articleTitle: Optimization Algorithm Research and Design of Chip Manufacturing Virtual System Based on SECS/GEM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In order to improve the production efficiency, improve the product quality and reduce the cost in the field of chip manufacturing, this paper designs a virtual system based on SECS/GEM protocol to simulate the real production process of chip manufacturing, so as to optimize each stage of chip manufacturing. The system includes a equipment-side program that simulates the equipment and a host-side program that interacts with it. The host-side can collect state data from the equipment and monitor the equipment. Secondly, in order to improve production efficiency, an optimization algorithm of job shop scheduling based on reinforcement deep learning is designed. Experiments show that the system can simulate the process of chip manufacturing to some extent, optimize and improve the manufacturing process, and improve the overall efficiency of the equipment.

articleTitle: Image Robust Watermarking Based on Improved Invariant Feature Matrix and Chaotic Map
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 17th International Conference on Anti-counterfeiting, Security, and Identification (ASID)
abstract: In this paper, a robust and secure watermarking approach using improved invariant feature matrix and chaotic map is proposed. The watermark is embedded into the host cover image for the purpose of authentication, annotation and copyright protection. The original cover image is not required for watermark extraction. For better confidentiality, we apply the chaos based Rijndael encryption algorithm and Hash-based message authentication codes on the double-value logic table in order to ensure the security of watermark information. Experimental results clearly indicated that the proposed scheme is highly robust and sufficient secure for various forms of attacks including common image processing and geometric attacks. Further, the performance evaluation of the proposed scheme is found better to existing state-of-the-art robust watermarking techniques under consideration. Furthermore, the construct of logic table considers not only the robustness against geometric attacks, but also the micro-variable sensitivity and uniqueness of the watermarked cover image.
